title: Hub: a Welcome too large with its tree goes with RatchetTreeOption distributionService; joiners fetch the tree by groupInfo with their leaf key
description:
Bug mimid-jvde; protocol-07 §5.5 (Welcome FanoutMessage carries a RatchetTreeOption), §5.6 (groupInfo); draft-ietf-mls-ratchet-tree-options-02 §3. Amends decision mimid-1wgh.6.12. Code: crates/mimid-server/src/hub/update.rs (step 11), hub/group_info.rs (steps 4 and 8), mimid-agent-core Agent::fetch_trees.

Mark 2026-11-21 (mimid-jvde): when the Welcome plus the full tree won't fit MAX_BODY_LEN, send the Welcome with a ratchet tree option that says to fetch the tree elsewhere; the newcomer fetches it via GroupInfo fetch. Details chosen by the agent:

1. Option. Readings: outOfBand(3) ("an unspecified out-of-band application protocol") or distributionService(4) ("reconstructed by the Distribution Service from the handshake"). Chosen: distributionService. The mimid hub is the DS and does rebuild the tree from the PublicMessage handshake (its Observer); protocol-07's FanoutMessage uses the tree-options RatchetTreeOption as is, so the option exists on the wire. httpsUrl was not considered: no tree URL endpoint exists.
2. When. full whenever the encoded Welcome FanoutMessage with the hub's tree is at most the limit (MAX_BODY_LEN; a test hook, Hub::with_body_limit, lowers it); no change for normal rooms. Otherwise distributionService.
3. Where the joiner gets it. POST /groupInfo/{roomId} (GroupInfo/fetch over JMAP, FetchGroupInfo on the live stream), the only protocol-07 endpoint that returns a tree. The joiner checks the response's room, group_id and epoch against its Welcome and joins with the full tree; the join verifies it against the Welcome's signed tree hash. The Welcome becomes an invite (InviteArrived) only after the fetch; a transient failure waits for the next receive, any other failure is a Problem and the Welcome is dropped.
4. Authorization. Readings: room policy as for an external join (canAddOwnClient etc.), or membership. Chosen: before the policy check, a request whose requestingSignatureKey is the signature key of a current leaf, and whose credential identity is that leaf's member identity, is answered; the request signature proves possession of the leaf key. The Commit is merged before the Welcome goes out, so the joiner's leaf is in the hub's tree. A member already holds the tree, so nothing leaks; anyone else still needs room policy. The agent signs this request with its identity key (mimi-mls Identity implements label::LabelSigner); its external-join requests keep a fresh key.
5. Too large both ways. The groupInfo response carries the same tree, so it is nearly as long as the full Welcome (measured: 1198 vs 1117 octets for one joining client, 1936 vs 2209 for four; the Welcome is longer only by about 118 octets per joining client minus about 200). If the Welcome without the tree, or the groupInfo response for the new epoch (built in full to measure it), is longer than the limit, the hub refuses the Commit (notAllowed, logged as welcome_too_large) before anything is written, instead of accepting members who can never join. A groupInfo response over the limit at fetch time (pending proposals grew it) is HubError::GroupInfoTooLarge: HTTP 422 group-info-too-large to peers, invalidArguments to a local JMAP or stream client.

Limitations: by-reference rescues only Welcomes within about 118 octets per joining client of the limit, so in practice a room whose tree reaches about 4 MiB takes no new members (a raise of the groupInfo response cap would change decision mimid-1wgh.6.67; not done). The hub serves only the current epoch, so a Commit between the Welcome and the fetch strands the joiner (Problem; re-invite). Spec gaps in mimid-3hoq (wg).
